issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires calculateTotalPrice to be static (shared across all instances) but the provided Solution implements calculateTotalPrice as an instance method and the Template's Main (example usage) calls it on an instance (shop.calculateTotalPrice(...)). This inconsistency will confuse students about whether to implement calculateTotalPrice as static or instance and may cause tests or example code to fail depending on the chosen implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to state calculateTotalPrice is an instance method (and update any wording about static usage), or (B) change the Solution and the example in Main to implement and call calculateTotalPrice as a static method (e.g., SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(meal)). Ensure the UML, the textual description, the template comments, and the solution all agree on the static vs instance nature of calculateTotalPrice.

issues.description: The problem statement initially describes the stock attribute as a final Stock instance (read-only after construction) assigned per saloon instance, but later explicitly states the stock attribute must be static (shared across all SealSaloon instances). This is an internal contradiction in the specification that will confuse students about whether stock should be shared or per-instance. The Solution chooses static, while the earlier description suggests non-static final.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify whether stock is shared across all SealSaloon instances or is per-instance. Update the problem statement (and UML if necessary) to state the intended design (either final per-instance or static shared) and ensure the template/example and solution follow the same choice. If stock should be shared, explicitly state it in the earlier attribute description; if it should be per-instance, remove the later 'must be static' note and adjust the Solution accordingly.
